title: Rigby2D update: Public Beta, v0.3.3
author: Scared-Sandwich1283
selftext:
Hey everyone, back with another Rigby2D update!

Since my last post, I've pushed Rigby2D through versions 0.3.0 to 0.3.3. A lot has changed, and the biggest step is that Rigby2D is moving beyond individual character animation into complete scene creation.

Here's what I've been working on:

* **Scene composition:** Bring multiple characters, animation clips, dialogue audio, layered backgrounds, parallax and camera movement together in one scene.
* **Timeline editing:** Trim and split clips, adjust playback speed, loop animations and crossfade between clips.
* **Automatic lip-sync (viseme):** Generate lip-sync from audio using local Whisper transcription, with support for nine mouth shapes.
* **Rendering:** Export scenes to PNG sequences, transparent WebM and MP4 with audio.
* **Runtime integration:** Play composed scenes through the JavaScript and Rust runtimes, with a dedicated Godot `RigbyScene2D` node.
* **AI workflows:** MCP tools for AI assistants to inspect, validate and edit rigs, animations and scenes.
* **Editor improvements:** Better transform guides, draw-order editing, resizable panels, searchable shortcuts, recent projects and improved documentation.

There's also AutoRig, animation retargeting, Python scripting and Spine skeleton import support, including binary `.skel` files.

I've moved Rigby2D into **public beta** and am working on the Windows release pipeline and code signing.

To show what the scene workflow looks like in practice, I've put together the NILA promo featuring NILA and Rigbytron.

**Watch the promo:** [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3StZlHwZeSo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3StZlHwZeSo)

Try it in the browser: [https://jaisurya-dev-art.github.io/rigby2d/](https://jaisurya-dev-art.github.io/rigby2d/)

Source and releases: [https://github.com/jaisurya-dev-art/rigby2d](https://github.com/jaisurya-dev-art/rigby2d)

Rigby2D is open source under MIT. If you're working on 2D games, animation or short films, give it a try and let me know what you think. Feedback is always welcome!
